 Nutson's Weekly Auto News Wrapup November 1, 2026
 The Auto Channel — Trusted automotive reporting for 32 years. This article is part of The Auto Channel’s independent automotive coverage library — one of the longest-running automotive publications 
online (since 1995). Our editors test, research, and document vehicles, technologies, recalls, and ownership experiences to help drivers make informed decisions.
 Unlike short news blurbs, our content is written for long-term usefulness — explaining what the vehicle is, why it matters, and how it affects real owners.
 Coverage includes reviews, specifications, safety data, recall history, industry context, and real-world driving impressions collected over decades of reporting.
AUTO CENTRAL – Louisville, KY: November 1, 2026; Every Sunday for over 30 years, 
 Larry Nutson - The Chicago Car Guy and Executive 
Producer of The Auto Channel - has delivered his weekly take on the automotive world. Each report distills the week’s top stories into sharp, easy-to-digest News Nuggets.
The full version of today’s News Nuggets — along with hundreds of thousands of additional articles, reviews, and editorial insights — can be found in The Auto Channel’s Million-Page Automotive 
Library, built and indexed over three decades. To dive deeper, simply copy any headline and paste it into this or any Site Search box on The Auto Channel. 
 LEARN MORE FROM THE WEB'S LONGEST RUNNING AUTOMOTIVE COLUMN 
 Here are Larry's Top Auto Story Picks of the Week of October 25 - October 31, 2026. Larry picked these as important, relevant, interesting, and sometimes semi-secret stories you need to know - served up 
as snappy, opinionated, and insider-sharp. These are expertly crafted, easy-to-understand news nuggets that cut through the noise and get right to what matters to you in the automotive world.
 * October sales forecast. October new-vehicle sales are expected to finish higher than last month and last year, while maintaining the sales path held for most of the year. Despite declining consumer sentiment, the 
seasonally adjusted annual rate, or SAAR, is expected to finish near 16.1 million. This is up from last month's 16 million pace and last year's 15.7 million level. According to Cox Automotive's forecast, sales volume is 
expected to rise 3.6% from last month and 7.2% from last year. There are large seasonal adjustments that make monthly comparisons challenging. October has 28 selling days, three more than last month and one more than last 
year. More selling days this month should lead to notably higher sales than in September. However, historically, the sales pace also slows in October, which will mitigate some of the expected increase. 
 * Used car price trends. Carfax reports the average asking price for used Hybrids (HEVs) & Electric Vehicles (BEVs) continues to drop. But, with gas prices remaining high because of the war with Iran, some used Hybrids 
and BEVs are selling for more than new 2026 models. 
 Learn more here .
 * GM sold your data. General Motors will pay $220 million to settle "allegations that it illegally sold drivers' private behavior and location data to brokers", who then sold the information to insurers that used it to 
set and sometimes increase rates. The settlement resolves claims by the attorneys general of 35 US states and the District of Columbia over the automaker's Smart Driver program, which enrolled millions of drivers "between 
2016 and its discontinuation in 2024. Other regulators have also reviewed GM's handling of driver data. GM was accused of pitching Smart Driver to help "people improve their personal driving safety, only to violate 
drivers' privacy by reneging on its "promise not to sell their data without permission." 
 * World Car Awards and London International Motor Show. The World Car Awards will announce its 2027 Top Three in the World finalists at the London International Motor Show on Friday, 26 February 2027, bringing a key 
point in the world's number one automotive awards programme to the UK capital. The announcement will reveal the final three contenders for World Car of the Year, World Urban Car, World Luxury Car, World Performance 
Car and World Car Design of the Year. The 2027 World Car Person of the Year will also be announced at the event. Both announcements will take place at ExCeL London on the opening day of the London International Motor 
Show, which runs from 26 to 28 February 2027. Also at the show, the World Car Awards stand will showcase the 2026 World Car Awards winners, giving visitors the opportunity to see the cars recognized by World Car's 
international jurors as attention turns to the contenders for 2027. The London International Motor Show will bring together vehicle manufacturers, technology companies, the automotive media and car buyers. Alongside 
new vehicle displays, visitors can look forward to test drives and live discussions, with areas dedicated to future technology, luxury cars and classics. .
 * Will EVs replace horse-drawn carriages? The New York City Council has voted to ban horse-drawn carriages in Central Park by June 2028, prompting discussions about alternative transportation options, including electric 
vehicles (BEVs) proposed by some carriage drivers. This decision follows concerns over animal welfare and safety incidents involving the carriages. The transition to BEVs could affect the livelihoods of current carriage 
drivers, who may need to adapt to new business models. New York City is the latest major metropolitan area that's voted to ban horse-drawn carriages. Over the last five years, cities including Philadelphia, Chicago and 
San Antonio, have outlawed the practice. .
 * Cars at Chicago's Griffin Museum of Science + Industry. "Cars That Moved America" explores how 20th century vehicles have changed the way we move, live and imagine what's next. Get an up-close look at more than 20 cars 
from the Richard H. Driehaus Automobile Collection, and explore the automobile in a whole new way, not just as a machine, but as a representation of the human experience. Featured cars include: 1926 Miller Locomobile, 
which raced in the Indianapolis 500, 1941 Chrysler Thunderbolt, dubbed "the car of the future" at the time, 1954 Mercury XM-800, a one-of-a-kind concept car that debuted at the Detroit Auto Show, and 1957 Ford Thunderbird 
E Code, the final iteration of the first generation, two-seat Thunderbird. 
 Learn how to visit here .
 * Toyota recall. Toyota is recalling 228,367 units of its 2022 to 2026 Toyota Sienna minivan models in the United States due to an issue with the second-row seat backs, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety 
Administration. According to the recall notice, the seat backs may fail to remain secured in the event of a crash, which may fail to properly protect an occupant, increasing the risk of injury. .
 * Porsche recall. Porsche is expanding an earlier recall that was first reported in October 2024. The recall affects Porsche vehicles with center-lock wheels. A supplier traceability investigation found that an additional 
548 vehicles were affected. Affected models include: 2024 Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS, 2024 Porsche 911 S/T, 2024 Porsche 911 Carrera GTS and 2024 Porsche 718 Spyder RS. The recalled vehicles were built with center-lock 
wheel fastening components manufactured outside specifications. As a result, the center-locking component could fracture, potentially causing a wheel to detach or reduced steering control. .
 * Koenigsegg. All seven of the U.S.-allocated 1185-horsepower Koenigsegg CC850s are being recalled over a faulty parking brake, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. The recall, filed on 
October 21, 2026, covers every CC850 unit delivered to the U.S. and focuses on an electronic parking brake that won't engage while the vehicle is in reverse. Only 70 units of the 1185-horsepower Koenigsegg CC850 are 
planned to built. .
 * World Rally in US. Knoxville, Tennessee will host the FIA World Rally Championship's U.S. return Aug. 26–29, 2027, the series' first American event since 1988. The rally will span Tennessee and Kentucky, with route 
details still to come. The rally service park, team base and fan festival are planned for World's Fair Park and Convention Centre in Knoxville. The ceremonial start is set for Lower Broadway in Nashville before the rally 
heads east to Knoxville. Routes pending Stages are expected to cross 15 counties, from the Appalachian Mountains to the Cumberland Plateau. Organizers plan to announce routes in early 2027. .
 * RIP. Jerry Palmer, a celebrated, retired American automotive designer who served as the Executive Director of Design for General Motors (GM) North American Operations, has died. Over a prolific career spanning more 
than three decades, Palmer heavily influenced the visual landscape of modern American sports and muscle cars, most notably through his defining work on the Chevrolet Corvette and Camaro lines. Palmer was 84.
 Stay safe. Be Well.
 Kind regards, 
Larry Nutson, the Chicago Car Guy
